evidence: PMLR v202 page (Pei, Bieber, Shi, Sutton, Yin; ICML 2023) abstract: scratchpad approach yields invariants of 'quality comparable to those obtained by a dynamic analysis tool with access to five program traces'.
correction: Claim should name the scratchpad variant (sequential prediction) and the dynamic tool comparison is Daikon-style; exact title: 'Can Large Language Models Reason about Program Invariants?'

evidence: Abstract: 'Our findings show that LLM-based test generation approaches mainly capture the actual program behavior making bug detection difficult.' arXiv title (v2, revised Oct 2026) is now 'Can we find bugs using LLM-generated oracles?'
correction: Title: 'Can we find bugs using LLM-generated oracles?' (arXiv 2410.21136 v2; v1 title differed). Authors Konstantinou, Degiovanni, Papadakis. Also note abstract: LLM oracles have higher fault-detection potential than EvoSuite's.

evidence: ASE 2025 page (Molinelli, Di Grazia, Martin-Lopez, Ernst, Pezze): 'experimenting with 13,866 test oracles that we mined from 135 Java projects'; LLMs reach 'a mutation score comparable to the score of human-designed test oracles'.
correction: Full title: 'Do LLMs Generate Useful Test Oracles? An Empirical Study with an Unbiased Dataset'. Abstract also notes LLMs struggle with complex oracles.

evidence: Abstract: 'When it does generate an assertion oracle, more than 47% of them are false positives, and the true positive assertions only increase fault detection by 0.3%'. No 19/57 figure in abstract.
correction: Authors Hossain, Filieri, Dwyer, Elbaum, Visser; venue ESEC/FSE 2023 (doi 10.1145/3611643.3616265). Drop the 19/57 figure unless found in body text; abstract only states TOGA originally detected 57 bugs.

evidence: SCP 69 (2007) 35-45, Ernst et al. abstract: 'Dynamic invariant detection runs a program, observes the values that the program computes, and then reports properties that were true over the observed executions.'
correction: 'template' is not in the abstract; the checked properties come from a grammar of invariant types (examples list in abstract).

evidence: Sec. 4.2: '--conf_limit ... filters out invariants that are satisfied purely by chance ... Daikon never outputs invariants that were ever false ... default is .99'; a<b confidence '1 - 1/2^numsamples'. Sec. 5.4.1 is 'Redundant invariants'.
correction: Location: Sec. 4.2 'Options to control invariant detection' only (not 5.4.1). Manual describes Daikon 5.9.0, Sept 1 2026.

evidence: ACM TOSEM 23(4), 2014, Nguyen, Kapur, Weimer, Forrest; abstract contains 'instead of using traces to filter out predefined templates' (infers invariants directly from traces).

Lemieux & Beschastnikh abstract: 'a tool to dynamically mine temporal specifications in LTL from traces'; Sec. I: instances 'matching a user-defined temporal property type'. Support/confidence shown in Sec. III stack example (support 654, confidence 0.0796).
correction: Title: 'Investigating Program Behavior Using the Texada LTL Specifications Miner' (ASE 2015 tool demo). Support/confidence location is Sec. III, not abstract/Sec. I.
